extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, their counsel, and USPTO OED/enforcement staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and orders governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO when a practitioner is disciplined by a State authority, including suspension terms, notification, and administrative actions to dissociate practitioner access. Focused on applying 37 C.F.R. §11.24 and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal suspension under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24(b), the Director may suspend a practitioner from practice before the USPTO where reciprocal discipline is appropriate based on a state disciplinary order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order suspends Respondent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO for violation of 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h), predicated upon being indefinitely suspended from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State. Authority cited: 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline may be predicated upon violations of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct such as §11.804(h) when based on state-imposed suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter the USPTO suspension is predicated on the Supreme Court of Ohio's indefinite suspension for violations of Ohio Rules of Professional Conduct 8.4(b) and 8.4(h) arising from criminal convictions; the order explicitly ties the USPTO sanction to the state finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum suspension term (two years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for a minimum of two (2) years from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states suspension is effective the date of the Final Order and that no petition for reinstatement may be filed within two years of the Final Order. The two-year minimum is stated as consistent with Ohio Gov. Bar R. V, Section 25(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing petition for reinstatement within two years
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO in the specified matters may be filed within two years of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order expressly provides that Respondent shall not apply for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.60 within two years from the date of this Final Order; this mirrors state rule preventing petitions within two years of an indefinite suspension order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of suspension notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided template notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs the OED Director to publish the specified 'Notice of Suspension' which identifies the respondent, registration number, the nature of the suspension, the regulatory provision violated (37 C.F.R. §11.804(h)), the predicate state suspension, and the reinstatement restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must state respondent identity and registration, the suspension (scope and minimum duration), regulatory basis, predicate state action and reasons, and the reinstatement restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template notice included in the Final Order provides verbatim content to be materially matched: identification of respondent and registration number; statement of two-year minimum suspension for violating 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h) predicated on state indefinite suspension; reference to Gov. Bar. R. V, Section 25(A); citation to the state opinion and summary of misconduct (e.g., criminal convictions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs dissemination of the discipline and reasons to relevant state agencies and courts, ensuring official communication beyond the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. §11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. §11.58 following public discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the order does not enumerate §11.58 duties, it requires compliance with that regulation (which typically includes notice to clients, file transfer instructions, and other obligations imposed on disciplined practitioners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of respondent's name from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative action to remove practitioner identifying information and PKI linkage to prevent representation or electronic filings under associated credentials while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on obtaining or being added to USPTO Customer Numbers until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order expressly bars any new Customer Number applications or additions to existing Customer Numbers during the suspension period prior to reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline appropriate when no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a respondent does not contest reciprocal discipline or when there is no genuine issue of material fact under §11.24(d), the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states that because Respondent 'does not contest reciprocal discipline' it was determined there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d), and reciprocal suspension for a minimum of two years is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and public access to disciplinary decisions (35 U.S.C. §32; OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary actions are taken pursuant to statutory/regulatory authority and are made available for public review via the OED FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24 as authority and provides the FOIA Reading Room URL where disciplinary decisions are available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certificate of service for Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be mailed/served (here: by certified mail, return receipt requested) to respondent's counsel, with a certificate of service filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document includes a Certificate of Service stating the Final Order was mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to Respondent's Counsel and includes addresses and dates; demonstrates procedural requirement for notice.
